clauses.clause: Listen to the ideas of others during discussions and projects.
clauses.note: Students listen to partner ideas during planning discussion

clauses.clause: Provide feedback to others in discussions and shared projects.
clauses.note: Students provide feedback to peers on their writing using the Pinky Partners protocol

verdicts.evidence: Invite students to turn and talk with their partner: 'What do you want to write in verse 3? Why?' (Answers will vary.)
verdicts.rationale: Students contribute ideas, listen to others, and provide feedback throughout the lesson. In Work Time A, students contribute ideas in partner discussions ('What do you want to write in verse 3? Why?') and listen to each other ('remind them to show respect for one another's ideas by listening intently and taking turns to speak'). In Work Time C, students provide feedback using the Pinky Partners protocol ('Tell students they are going to use the Pinky Partners protocol to provide feedback on their partners' writing').
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Contribute to discussions and shared projects by offering ideas, listening to the ideas of others, and providing feedback. (I/C)

clauses.clause: Communicate ideas clearly when presenting.
clauses.note: Students communicate ideas clearly when sharing observations about the poem

clauses.clause: Present information in an organized manner.
clauses.note: Students present feedback in an organized manner using sentence starters

clauses.clause: Express ideas and information clearly through speech.
clauses.note: Students express ideas clearly in partner discussions about the poem

verdicts.evidence: Select two to three students to share out the aspects of high-quality work they noticed.
verdicts.rationale: Students communicate clearly to present ideas, information, and texts throughout the lesson. In Opening A, students share observations about high-quality writing ('Select two to three students to share out the aspects of high-quality work they noticed') and discuss with partners ('What is something you saw or heard in the poem that let you know the poem is high quality?'). In Work Time C, students present feedback in an organized manner using sentence starters ('remind them to be kind, specific, and helpful and to use the sentence starters'). In Closing A, students share reflections on the feedback process.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Communicate clearly to present ideas, information, and texts. (I/C)
